definition: A robust outlier score using median and median absolute deviation instead of mean and standard deviation — resistant to the outliers it detects.
details: A robust outlier score using median and median absolute deviation instead of mean and standard deviation — resistant to the outliers it detects.

explainer.lead: A robust outlier score that uses the median and median absolute deviation instead of the mean and standard deviation. It is resistant to the outliers it detects, unlike the standard z-score.

tiers.eli5: Like judging who is unusually tall by comparing to the middle person in the room rather than an average skewed by one giant.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for anomaly detection when data may contain extreme values that would distort mean and standard deviation. A pitfall is applying it to clean, symmetric data where the standard z-score is simpler and conventional.
tiers.paperLevel: The modified z-score is computed as 0.6745 times the deviation from the median divided by the median absolute deviation; it is robust, though thresholds must be chosen and constant data can break the denominator.

explainer.example: A sensor reading is flagged as an outlier because its modified z-score exceeds a chosen threshold, even though a few extreme readings would have skewed the mean.
